1dc608f14f3aee21.title: Malibu Library Speaker Series: Jeffrey Marlow — In-Person Program
1dc608f14f3aee21.desc: The Malibu Library Speaker Series presents Marine microbiologist and explorer Dr. Jeffrey Marlow at Malibu Library on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 7 pm. Dr. Marlow offers a new perspective on the power and beauty of the deep sea in his first book, The Dark Frontier: Unlocking the Secrets of the Deep Sea. He illuminates the ocean’s scientific marvels, including microbes that breathe metal and fish that withstand crushing pressures, as well as theories about how underwater habitats may have been the cradle of life on Earth. He will reveal the deep sea’s microbial universes, worlds within worlds that have opened new possibilities of survival in extreme environments. Dr. Marlow is an Assistant Professor of Biology at Boston University, where his lab studies the links between microbes and their surroundings in a range of extreme environments. He has led or participated in 10 deep-sea research expeditions and worked on the science team of three of NASA's Mars rover missions. He has served as a science advisor at the United Nations' negotiations for the High Seas Treaty and is a member of the National Academies of Sciences New Voices leadership program. Additionally, he is a National…

1d16aec8fd4e4027.title: Virtual Book Club Discusses "Crux" by Gabriel Tallent — Virtual Program
1d16aec8fd4e4027.desc: We read 1/4 of the book each week. Below is the breakdown for the weekly discussion: November 3: Part 1 - The Princess - Pages 3 - 71 November 10: Part 2 - Intersection - Pages 75 - 161 November 17: Part 3 - Isolation - Pages 165 - 273 November 24: Parts 4 & 5 - Wonderland & Exposure - Pages 277 to the end of the book "Dan and Tamma are two teenagers in their last year of high school in the southern Mojave Desert. One is a gifted golden child, the other a mouthy burnout. Climbing boulders in trash-strewn parking lots during cold desert nights, they seal their unique bond and dream of a life of adventure. As the year progresses and adult reality looms, they are rocked by change and pulled apart by irreconcilable obligations. Differences of class, talent, and prospects take on new importance; options dwindle, and their decisions grow ever more consequential and perilous. It feels inevitable, finally, that something must give. With a magnificent gift for nature writing and a joyful appreciation for the redemptive power of friendship, Gabriel Tallent gives readers a rollicking, adrenaline-filled, and soul-searching novel about risking everything to change your life." -- Provided by…

1d7d291443dd6bf6.title: Community Book Club: The Authenticity Project by Clare Pooley — In-Person Program
1d7d291443dd6bf6.desc: A solitary green notebook brings together six strangers and leads to unexpected friendship, and even love. Julian Jessop, an eccentric, lonely artist and septuagenarian believes that most people aren't really honest with each other. But what if they were? And so he writes--in a plain, green journal--the truth about his own life and leaves it in his local café. It's run by the incredibly tidy and efficient Monica, who furtively adds her own entry and leaves the book in the wine bar across the street. Before long, the others who find the green notebook add the truths about their own deepest selves--and soon find each other in real life at Monica's café. The Authenticity Project is just a tonic for our times, a book that readers will take to their hearts and read with unabashed pleasure. Regular print copies will be available at the reference desk. E-book, and e-audiobook versions are available within our system.
